## Historical audit — S0080

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/ablation_r1/ours_without_regression_guidance/C1/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`. Citations below refer to JSONL lines in this file. Only chunk 1 of 2 is visible; neither the reference nor the renders is independently visible in this audit.

| Evidence | Observed operations and limits |
|---|---|
| Goal | The request was to reconstruct an indoor photograph with separate meshes and matching camera, framing, colors and materials. The student interpreted it as a ship compartment; that scene identification is the student’s inference, not an independently checked image observation (lines 1, 3). |
| Initial build | Step 1 constructed multiple semantic groups: architecture, three-tier bunks, cabinets, lockers, chair, workbench, wall equipment, bench, pipes and lamps. Colored primitives, deck seams and a global roughness setting supplied appearance; no image texture was used in the visible code. Chair parts were grouped, and supports were positioned explicitly, but hierarchy and claimed contact do not independently establish physical connections or correct pose (lines 3–4). |
| Camera exploration | After receiving the step-1 render, the student reported a low lamp, central post and small rear furniture, then hypothesized that longer focal length and a lower viewing direction would improve framing. Step 2 changed lens 23.5 to 31.5 and camera target; it also enabled denoising, so the code was not literally camera-only. The stated expected effects were hypotheses, not measured results (lines 7–10). |
| Appearance exploration | The student claimed step 2 improved post placement while lamp and bunk positions still differed. Step 3 retained that camera and changed colors, ambient and area lighting, point lights, roughness and lamp emission to seek darker, more localized illumination (lines 13–16). No procedural surface texture is evident in this code. |
| Validation and selection | All three execution results report `ok: true` and saved render images and blend files; selection events subsequently recorded steps 1, 2 and 3 respectively (lines 5–6, 11–12, 17–18). The runner logs show 16 samples despite code requesting 32. These are **formal execution successes**, not proof of visual or geometric correctness. The final overall submission and any later review are unknown. |
| Guidance | The visible input includes general system instructions and a repeated runner review prompt asking for one correction family and preservation of groups (lines 1, 7, 13). The camera-family revision is consistent with that prompt. No distinct teacher diagnosis, proposed update, receipt or adoption is shown in this chunk; the directory name alone is not evidence of teacher input. |

**Assessment and uncertainty.** The visible work is autonomous student reconstruction and iterative exploration, with three nonempty executed builds. There is no visible algorithm failure, empty patch or technical interruption. Final task correctness is **unknown**, not established by successful renders or the student’s landmark claim. In particular, object visibility and occlusion, actual part contacts, object pose, texture fidelity, lighting quality and camera match cannot be checked without the images or geometric inspection. The hypothesis that excess ambient/frontal light caused the main remaining disagreement also remains unverified here.

**Lessons:** Separating a camera revision from an appearance revision makes changes easier to interpret, although enabling denoising concurrently confounds a pure camera comparison. The specific post, bunk and illumination hypotheses are task-specific; semantic grouping and checking actual contacts and rendered visibility are transferable practices, not verified outcomes in this record.
